text: The coffee has no bottom. I respect that.
Needed Form 27-B to file for Form 27-B.
Hold music is one flute, forever. Honestly a vibe.
My soul was stamped so gently. Would be processed again.
Lights flicker whenever I think about my life choices.
Waited so long my review is also late. Sorry.
Staff gave me a free paperclip. Best day since the funeral.
The printer jammed on my own obituary. Rude.
Everyone smiled. Nobody had a face, but they smiled.
Clipboards everywhere. No pens. Classic.
The queue has a queue. I'm in the second one.
The office fern is thriving. Unlike me. Five stars.
Found my file. It was under 'Misc. Eternity'. Fine.
The little bell sound made my whole afterlife.
I am not dead. Please advise. Also please stop stamping me.
Snacks cost one memory each. Fair trade.
Chair has been wobbling since 1974. So have I.
Got four memos telling me to ignore the fifth memo.
Staff were very professional, for the dead.
It's fine. It's an office. It's forever.
Elevator music only plays the middle of songs.
Found a sticky note saying 'You did great.' Not sure who left it.
Lobby chairs are excellent. Wish I had a body to sit in them.
Now serving number 4. For the last nine years.
Pulled a ticket. It said 'Congratulations.' Unclear why.
The pen is chained to the desk. So am I, apparently.
Warm welcome, clear signs, one free biscuit. Dying was worth it.
Please tick one box: Alive, Dead, Unsure. I ticked Unsure.
The greeter said 'Welcome to the end!' with real energy.
Badge photo made me look alive. Will not be sharing.
Harp music nonstop. Lovely for an hour. It's been a century.
Clouds are softer than advertised. Zero complaints.
Halo sizing was a nightmare. Mine slides over one eye.
Gate is pearly, queue is orderly, clipboard is shiny.
The temp choir sang 'Happy Birthday' at my arrival. I died in March.
Free wing fitting! Bit drafty but very chic.
Petra has the keys but not the list. We waited together. We bonded.
So peaceful I forgot what I was worried about. Five stars.
It is a dry heat. Still a heat.
Lava lamp in the lobby is a nice touch. Also real lava.
Their HR department is somehow worse than my last one.
Pitchforks are ergonomic now. Management really listens.
Infinite paperwork. At least the paper is warm.
My caseworker was a demon named Brad. Very supportive.
Asked about air conditioning. Everyone laughed. Then I laughed. Then we all sweated.
Held a fire drill. Everyone just stood there. Reasonable.
Waited 300 years in Limbo. The vending machine only takes souls.
Can't see the desk through the fog, but the fog is friendly.
Told me 'maybe' and honestly that was more than I expected.
Sign says 'Next window.' All the windows say 'Next window.'
The clocks all show different times. All of them are 'later'.
Found a bench. Sat. Did nothing for ages. Perfect.
Door opens inward, outward and sometimes sideways. Mixed feelings.
Great acoustics. My complaint echoed back as a compliment.
Asked to come back as a cat. Got 'a similar mammal.' Fine.
Wheel of rebirth stuck on 'pigeon' for 40 minutes.
Returned as a golden retriever. Reviewing from the park. Perfect.
Got my old life back. Same debts. Same landlord.
Counter staff said 'See you next time!' and meant it literally.
They mixed up my paperwork. I'm told it's temporary. For a lifetime.
Free juice before reincarnation. Tasted like a past life.
Left with a glow and a fresh start. Great service.
The feast never ends. My belt, however, did. Five stars.
Mead was fresh, the bench was wide, the shouting was heartfelt.
Shield rack was full. Mine was the squeaky one.
Too many horns blowing. Nobody agrees on what they mean.
Valkyrie gave me a lift and a clipboard. Class act.
Wanted glorious battle. Got a glorious waiting list.
